content.text:
I identified mp-1222825 (Lu4Zr3O12) as the only phase present.

- **Match:** Its simulated pattern lines up closely with the observed one. The peaks fall at about 14.4, 18.6 and 22.6°. There is a strong doublet at 30.0/30.9°, close in height to the observed 100/86. Further peaks sit at 34.5/35.4, 46.4/47.3 and 57.5/58.5°, and their relative intensities are similar to the observed ones.
- **Rejected candidates:** I also simulated the two double perovskites (Pr2ZnPtO6, Sm2MnRhO6) and CrAuO2. None of them gives the observed peak positions, and the perovskites have nothing at 14.4 or 18.6°.
- **Not checked:** I did not simulate the other five candidates, so they are ruled out only by the near-complete fit of Lu4Zr3O12.
- **Unexplained peaks:** A few weak features (about 24° and 42°, around 5% intensity) are not accounted for. They are too weak and sparse to justify a second phase.
